summary: stood under the station's scheduled weather while the sprinkler rig played rain
lines: Scheduled weather on the concourse — ten minutes of sprinkler rain, oddly convincing.
The station runs its rain program. Half the dock stops to stand in it.
Artificial rain day. You let it soak the jacket like the real thing.

summary: got caught behind the dockworkers' guild procession, banners and brass
lines: The dockworkers' guild parades the promenade — banners, brass, no freight moves for an hour.
Guild procession blocks the ramp. You learn the words to their anthem by the third pass.
Brass band, union banners, a stalled cargo line. Nobody minds much.

summary: rode out a station-wide brownout by candlelight in the cantina
lines: Grid brownout — the cantina lights candles like it's a tradition. It might be.
The lights die for twenty minutes. Someone starts a sing-along. The dark fixes itself.
Brownout sweeps the ring. Emergency lamps and unbothered bartenders.

summary: listened to a busker play a stringbox older than the station
lines: A busker by the lifts coaxes real music out of a stringbox held together with tape.
The same three songs all afternoon from the concourse busker. They're good songs.
Stringbox busker at the junction — you stay for one more than you meant to.

summary: ate at the noodle stand every spacer on this ring swears by
lines: The noodle stand by berth row: one pot, one recipe, no complaints ever filed.
You find the noodle stand the dockhands queue at. The queue is correct.
Hot broth at the rail while the freight cranes swing. Good watch.

summary: spent half an hour walking a lost tourist back to the passenger ring
lines: A tourist deep in the freight ring, map upside-down. You walk them home.
Lost passenger on the cargo decks — you point them at daylight and civilization.
Half an hour of wrong turns returned to the passenger ring. They wave from the lift.

summary: paid a correction fee for a manifest line some clerk fat-fingered
lines: A clerk's typo becomes your correction fee: {credits}.
Manifest line 14 says you imported yourself. Fixing it costs {credits}.
The paperwork error was theirs; the fee, naturally, is yours: {credits}.

summary: endured a berth neighbour running engine diagnostics through the sleep cycle
lines: The next berth runs drive diagnostics all night. You learn its resonance by heart.
Your neighbour's engine whine finds the one frequency the bulkhead loves.
Sleep cycle, interrupted: somebody's turbine has opinions.

summary: found a recruiting poster featuring a ship the same class as their own, heroically clean
lines: A recruiting poster shows your ship's class gleaming like it never hauled a ton. Lies, lovely lies.
Your hull's twin stars in a navy poster by the lifts. Yours has more character.
The poster ship has no patch welds. You pity its crew.

summary: floated for two glorious seconds when the ring's gravity hiccuped
lines: Grav plate hiccup — two seconds of float, one spilled tray, scattered applause.
The ring skips a beat and everyone's coffee learns to fly.
Brief zero-g on the promenade. The old hands don't even drop their cards.

summary: shuffled through a station fire drill with a few hundred unimpressed spacers
lines: Fire drill: the whole ring files to the assembly points, complaining in unison.
Klaxons, orange vests, a headcount. The drill ends; the grumbling doesn't.
You now know where muster point C-7 is. You will never need it.

summary: found the one kiosk on the ring that brews actual coffee
lines: Real coffee, real beans, third kiosk down. You memorize the location like a wormhole.
The kiosk by the chandlery brews the genuine article. The day improves.
Actual coffee discovered. You tell no one. Some intel stays personal.

summary: watched a no-paperwork auction move a freighter's worth of goods in twenty minutes
lines: A quiet auction in a loading bay: no docket numbers, no receipts, brisk bidding.
Twenty minutes, forty lots, zero paperwork. Efficient place, this.
The auctioneer's gavel is a wrench. The provenance is nobody's business.

summary: passed the unlicensed dental stall and kept walking, faster
lines: The corridor dentist has a queue. You upgrade your flossing resolve on the spot.
Unlicensed dentistry, walk-ins welcome. You walk on.
The sign says PAINLESS. The sounds say otherwise.

summary: paid the dock's unofficial 'berth insurance' to a very polite man
lines: A polite man explains berth insurance. You buy some: {credits}.
The local arrangement, explained with a smile: {credits} keeps your paint unscratched.
Berth insurance, cash only, no certificate issued: {credits}.

summary: got passed a counterfeit credit chit somewhere in the evening's changes
lines: One of tonight's credit chits is beautifully, worthlessly fake: {credits}.
A counterfeit chit surfaces in your change. Art, really. Expensive art: {credits}.
The chit scans fine twice, then never again: {credits}.

summary: watched loader-exo racing in a cargo bay after the shift bell
lines: After-hours loader races in bay nine. The fast one's pilot is maybe twelve.
Exo-loaders drag racing between container stacks. Security holds the stopwatch.
The cargo bay becomes a racetrack at shift's end. Nobody official notices, officially.

summary: sold a drawer of odds and ends at the no-questions pawn stall
lines: The pawn stall asks nothing and pays cash: {credits} for a drawer of mystery parts.
No-questions pawn: your junk drawer becomes {credits}.
The pawnbroker weighs your odds and ends like produce: {credits}.

summary: found the back-room book running odds on freighter arrival times
lines: There's a betting book on arrival times. The bookie knows the lanes better than traffic control.
Odds posted on every inbound hull. The smart money knows something about the 0400 packet.
Freighter arrival betting — the only timetable on this ring anyone trusts.

summary: browsed a market stall where every item still had someone else's name on it
lines: The stall sells 'pre-owned' goods, some still warm. You browse, hands in pockets.
Half this market fell off a freighter. The other half was pushed.
Goods of flexible provenance, priced to move. You admire and abstain.

summary: learned the patrol schedule is for sale at the cigarette kiosk
lines: The kiosk sells smokes, candy, and tonight's patrol route. Bundle pricing.
Security's rounds are public knowledge here — for a price, at the kiosk.
Patrol schedule, laminated, two credits. The law here is well organized; just not by the law.

summary: sampled whatever the maintenance crew distills behind the recycler
lines: The recycler-room still produces something technically drinkable. You survive a sample.
Maintenance brews behind the air plant. It tastes like solvent and friendship.
One cup of the unofficial house spirit. Your sinuses report full clearance.

summary: queued forty minutes to be told to queue elsewhere, with a stamped slip to prove it
lines: Window 4 sends you to window 9, with a stamp. Window 9 is proud of the stamp.
Forty minutes of queue earns a referral slip in triplicate. Civilization.
The queue here has a queue. Both are orderly. Neither is fast.

summary: watched customs disassemble somebody else's ship with surgical patience
lines: Customs takes a yacht apart panel by panel, two berths down. You feel very law-abiding.
Somebody else's inspection runs six hours. You alphabetize your own paperwork, just in case.
The inspection team works like surgeons. The yacht's owner ages visibly.

summary: sat through a mandatory dock-safety seminar, twice, due to a clerical error
lines: Mandatory safety seminar. A clerical error makes it doubly mandatory for you.
Two hours on tether discipline. The presenter's enthusiasm is the real hazard.
Dock safety, the seminar, the sequel. Your attendance is now exemplary.

summary: got cited by an enforcement drone for an improperly coiled umbilical
lines: An enforcement drone photographs your umbilical coil and issues judgement: {credits}.
Citation: hose coiled counter-regulation. The drone is not open to debate: {credits}.
The drone's ticket prints before you finish arguing: {credits}.

summary: walked a promenade so clean it echoed
lines: The promenade gleams. Somewhere, a scuff mark is being interrogated.
Not one sticker, stain, or stray bolt. The cleanliness is faintly unnerving.
You could eat off this deck. A posted notice prohibits doing so.

summary: got thoroughly approved of by a customs sniffer-beagle
lines: The customs beagle inspects you and finds you delightful. Highest honor this port gives.
Sniffer dog, official vest, deeply professional. It wags anyway. You pass.
Cleared by beagle. The handler notes your cooperation; the dog notes your lunch.

summary: discovered there is a permit for nearly everything here, including permits
lines: The licensing kiosk offers 214 permit categories. One is for operating the kiosk.
You browse the permit menu: busking, fishing, queueing (commercial). All stamped, all filed.
There is a permit for walking a cat on the promenade. You note it. Just in case.

summary: was politely escorted back to the licensed-visitor zone by two large officers
lines: Wrong corridor — two polite mountains in uniform walk you back to the visitor zone.
The restricted-area line is exactly where you found the two officers. Noted.
A courteous escort, a gentle lecture, a stamped advisory slip. Tight ship, this port.

summary: had a dropped credit chit returned by station security, with a receipt
lines: Security returns a chit you didn't know you'd dropped, with paperwork: {credits}.
Lost-and-found, fully itemized: your {credits} comes back with a case number.
An officer hands back your dropped chit and a form to sign. Honest place: {credits}.

summary: toured the bonded warehouse where cargo waits in numbered, climate-controlled dignity
lines: The bonded warehouse: ten thousand crates in perfect rows, each with a biography.
Cargo here is filed like literature. The warehouse master speaks of lot 7741 with feeling.
Climate-controlled, triple-sealed, alphabetized. Freight heaven, or its waiting room.

summary: watched the loaders' union take a strike vote in the open mess
lines: The loaders vote on striking, in public, loudly. The count is close. The mood isn't.
Strike vote in the mess hall — hands up, jaws set. Freight may get interesting.
Union meeting spills into the concourse. The word 'tomorrow' does heavy lifting.

summary: stepped around two dock crews arguing over a berth allocation at full volume
lines: Two crews dispute a berth at parade-ground volume. Bets are being taken.
A berth allocation argument enters its second hour. Security watches from a safe distance.
The shouting match has spectators now. You don't pick a side. Out loud.

summary: noticed the security patrols have doubled and stopped smiling
lines: Twice the patrols, half the small talk. The station is holding its breath.
Security walks in pairs now, hands near belts. Something's circling.
The patrol pattern tightened overnight. The old hands drink closer to their ships.

summary: passed the cantina's confiscation bin, freshly full
lines: The cantina's weapons bin filled up by midshift. Healthy sign, that is not.
A bin of confiscated knives by the cantina door, labelled THURSDAY.
The door policy is 'leave it in the bin.' The bin has had a busy week.

summary: hit the deck with everyone else when a pressure klaxon cried wolf
lines: Pressure klaxon — the whole concourse drops, then stands up pretending it didn't.
False alarm on deck seven. Everyone's casual about it a beat too late.
The klaxon lies, but nobody trusted it enough not to flinch.

summary: watched a freighter get clamped and impounded over somebody's unpaid something
lines: Clamps go on a freighter two rows over. Its crew negotiates at top volume.
An impound team works fast and silent. The freighter's captain does neither.
Yellow clamps, red faces. You double-check your own berth fees quietly.

summary: read the new curfew notice taped over the old curfew notice
lines: A fresh curfew notice, taped over last month's. The hours got shorter.
Curfew moved up an hour. The cantina adjusts by locking the door and continuing.
NEW HOURS, says the notice. The grumbling is station-wide and synchronized.

summary: watched a rumour empty the commissary shelves in an hour
lines: A shortage rumour hits the commissary — shelves stripped before the shift bell.
Panic buying, orderly but fast. The rumour was false; the empty shelves aren't.
Somebody said 'rationing' too loudly. The commissary is now a museum of shelving.

summary: fell asleep in the solarium with half the off-shift
lines: The solarium at midshift: a dozen spacers, all asleep, all pretending to read.
You doze under the sun lamps. Nobody wakes anybody here. House rule.
An hour of borrowed sunlight and shameless napping. The station approves.

summary: watched old-timers fish the reclamation pond, which contains no fish
lines: Three regulars fish the reclamation pond. It has never held fish. That's not the point.
Lines in the water, hats over eyes. The pond is fishless; the afternoon is perfect.
You ask what they're catching. 'Quiet,' says the nearest hat.

summary: kibitzed a chess game that has reportedly been running for three weeks
lines: The concourse chess game enters week three. Spectators bring their own chairs now.
One move was played today. The crowd discusses it like a wedding.
Chess at glacier speed by the lifts. You study the board and silently disagree with everyone.

summary: got taught a proper cargo hitch by a dockhand with strong opinions about knots
lines: An old dockhand corrects your hitch, twice, then teaches the real one. Knowledge transferred.
Twenty minutes on the difference between a hitch and a tragedy. Your lashings improve.
The knot lesson comes with history, philosophy, and one perfect loop.

summary: wandered a market where the loudest sound was the bread oven
lines: The afternoon market hums along — bread oven, low chatter, no hurry anywhere.
Stalls, steam, the smell of baking. Commerce at the pace of a nap.
You buy nothing and stay an hour. The market doesn't mind.

summary: heard the dockworkers' choir rehearsing in an empty cargo bay for the acoustics
lines: The dock choir rehearses in bay two for the echo. The echo is earning its keep.
Forty dockhands, four-part harmony, one empty bay. Better than the lottery, this port.
Choir practice rolls down the berth row. Work slows. Nobody fixes that.

summary: passed the ration queue that forms before the lights come up
lines: The ration line was there before dawn-cycle. It's longer than the freight queue.
Quiet faces, numbered chits, a line that moves slow and never shortens.
The station feeds everyone. Eventually. The queue is the price.

summary: walked a concourse where half the shopfronts are plated over
lines: Every other shopfront is welded shut. The survivors share customers and rumors.
The concourse echoes. Plated windows, FOR LEASE signs older than the dust on them.
Half a market, doubled hopes. The open stalls sweep their floors twice a day anyway.

summary: bought a trinket off a kid selling polished scrap by the lifts
lines: A kid sells scrap polished into small marvels. You buy one: {credits}.
Salvage jewellery, child labor rates, real craft. You pay better than asked: {credits}.
The trinket is a drive bearing made beautiful. Worth more than {credits}, honestly.

summary: browsed a pawnshop window full of working tools, which says everything
lines: The pawnshop window is all tools — good ones. Nobody pawns a wrench they expect to need.
Calibrated, cared-for, pawned. The window is a eulogy for somebody's trade.
Working tools behind pawn glass. The port's story in one display case.

summary: hired a day-laborer off the ramp line to help shift cargo, and paid fair
lines: You hire off the ramp line for an honest shift, fair rate: {credits}, word gets around (standing {standing}).
A day's help, a fair wage: {credits}. The line remembers who pays straight (standing {standing}).
Cargo shifted, wage paid square: {credits}. This port keeps score on that (standing {standing}).

summary: sat through the scheduled brownout the station calls 'conservation hour'
lines: Conservation hour: the ring dims to amber and everyone pretends it's cozy.
The lights drop on schedule. The cantina's candles aren't romantic, they're budgetary.
Power rationing, hour two. The dark here is organized, at least.

summary: found a fresh mural of green fields painted across a sealed cargo door
lines: Somebody painted ten metres of wheat field on a dead cargo door. It helps. Oddly.
A mural of fields nobody here has seen, on a door nothing opens. The paint is fresh.
Green fields on rusted steel. The artist signed it 'SOON.'

summary: heard the ore co-op is dumping stock to make dock fees
lines: The ore co-op needs fee money tonight — {commodity} going at −{discount} for ~{hours}h if you move quick.
Desperation pricing at the co-op: {commodity} −{discount} for ~{hours}h.
The co-op's books are bleeding; your {commodity} price benefits: −{discount}, ~{hours}h.

summary: got swept into the spillover of a freight-baron's gala on the upper ring
lines: A gala overflows the upper ring — champagne fountains, dock passes be damned.
Somebody's celebrating a tonnage record. The canapés reach the freight deck by midnight.
The party upstairs leaks music and confetti for six decks.

summary: ate dinner entirely from promenade free samples
lines: The promenade vendors compete in free samples. You dine like a thrifty king.
Sample trays every ten metres. Dinner: solved, in fourteen courses of one bite.
A booming port feeds you for free, one toothpick at a time.

summary: discovered this port's tipping culture the expensive way
lines: Everyone tips here. Everyone. The dock cat has a saucer for it: {credits}.
Service with a smile and an expectant pause: {credits} in tips by day's end.
The gratuity economy claims its due: {credits}.

summary: stood a while at a fountain running actual water, just because it could
lines: A fountain of real water, recycled but proud. The decadence of a port doing well.
Tonnes of potable water, arranged decoratively. The rim would riot. You watch it sparkle.
The fountain exists purely to show off. It succeeds.

summary: counted a dozen HIRING banners between the lift and the cantina
lines: Hiring banners on every bulkhead — signing bonuses, day one. The boom is real.
Twelve crews recruiting between here and the bar. The bonuses climb as you walk.
Help wanted, everywhere, urgently. The port can't shift its own success fast enough.

summary: sublet their berth for two hours to a desperate packet captain
lines: Berths are gold tonight — a packet captain rents your pad for two hours: {credits}.
Overbooked port, your empty pad, one quick handshake: {credits}.
You scoot over; a mail packet squeezes in: {credits} for the courtesy.

summary: watched festival fireworks burst silent outside the dome
lines: Fireworks outside the dome — silent blooms over the docking lanes. The port can afford it.
The festival barge spends a fortune in fifteen silent, gorgeous minutes.
Soundless fireworks over the approach lanes. The whole ring stops to look up.

summary: got out-bid into donating at a spacer-benevolent-fund auction
lines: The benevolent-fund auction finds your wallet: {credits}, for the retired-spacers' ward (standing {standing}).
You bid on a terrible painting for a good cause: {credits} (standing {standing}).
Charity auction, peer pressure edition: {credits} donated, name read aloud (standing {standing}).

summary: joined the nightly ritual of listening to the generator catch on the first try
lines: The whole outpost pauses for the generator restart. It catches. Quiet cheering.
Generator flips to night cycle — one cough, then the steady hum everyone was waiting for.
The outpost's heartbeat skips its nightly beat, then steadies. Conversation resumes.

summary: watched the whole outpost turn out for the monthly mail packet
lines: Mail day: every soul on the outpost at the dock, pretending not to hope.
The packet's running late and the whole port knows it to the minute.
Letters, parts, one birthday cake in a stasis box. Mail day delivers.

summary: was greeted by name by strangers, twice, before lunch
lines: Day two and the outpost knows your name, your ship, and your coffee order.
No anonymity out here — the dockmaster's kid waves at you by name.
Sixty residents, and all of them have already met you. Word travels at outpost speed.

summary: got the proud, unsolicited tour of the water reclaimer
lines: The engineer shows off the reclaimer like a firstborn. It is, you admit, very clean water.
Unsolicited reclaimer tour, complete with taste test. You survive and compliment.
Every outpost has one sacred machine. Here it makes the water. You pay your respects.

summary: got pulled into the outpost's communal dinner and put on dish duty
lines: Communal dinner, one long table, no refusals accepted. You wash up after (standing {standing}).
The outpost eats together. Tonight you're family, and family does dishes (standing {standing}).
Stew, bread, sixty chairs, one of them yours (standing {standing}).

summary: shared the arrivals hall with three generations of a family starting over
lines: A family unloads everything they own — carefully, like it's the last of it. It is. The haven takes them in.
Three generations and four crates in the arrivals hall. The intake clerk is gentle. Good port.
New arrivals get soup before paperwork here. You note the order of operations.

summary: heard the haven's hour-bells ring the all-clear it has rung for years
lines: The hour-bells ring the all-clear, same as every hour for years. Nobody stops hearing it.
Bells on the hour: all's well. The haven says it out loud so everyone can stop wondering.
The all-clear rings. Shoulders you didn't notice were tight come down a centimetre.

summary: took a volunteer shift sorting donations at the haven's intake
lines: Two hours sorting donation crates at intake. The haven notices who shows up (standing {standing}).
You stack blankets and label boxes with the volunteer crew (standing {standing}).
Intake needed hands; you had two (standing {standing}).

summary: checked their sidearm at the haven's weapons lockers like everyone else
lines: Weapons lockers at every gate, no exceptions, no arguments. The haven's one hard rule.
You check the sidearm. The clerk's seen captains, pirates, and admirals do the same.
The locker receipt is the haven's real passport. Everyone carries one.

summary: walked the garden dome where the haven grows quiet on purpose
lines: The garden dome: real soil, slow paths, a posted request for quiet. Honored, universally.
Green rows under glass. The haven grows vegetables and decompression in equal measure.
You walk the garden's long loop twice. Whatever you carried in weighs less on the way out.

summary: watched the commodity floor erupt over a futures fix
lines: The trading floor detonates over a futures number. Fortunes change hands by hand signal.
Shouting, gestures, a bell — the floor settles a fortune in ninety seconds flat.
You watch the pit work. It's a brawl with bookkeeping.

summary: stood in the crowd that reads the price boards like scripture
lines: A silent crowd watches the price boards tick. Somebody sighs; somebody else grins.
The boards update; the crowd inhales as one. Commerce as theatre.
Every flicker of the board moves somebody's whole week. You read along.

summary: got cornered by a broker with a deal that was, for once, half-decent
lines: A broker's pitch survives your skepticism: {commodity} at −{discount} for ~{hours}h.
Ten minutes of patter, one usable number: {commodity} −{discount}, ~{hours}h.
The broker earns the commission this time: {commodity} marked down −{discount} for ~{hours}h.

summary: read the plaque commemorating the single largest cargo ever moved through this port
lines: The tonnage-record plaque is polished daily. The number is genuinely absurd.
A brass plaque honors one heroic cargo. Dockhands touch it for luck.
The record tonnage is engraved in brass and argued about in every bar.

summary: took shore leave downwell just to stand on actual grass
lines: Shuttle down, boots off, real grass. Worth every credit of the fare.
An hour downwell on living ground. The green stays in your eyes all shift.
Grass, wind, unrecycled air. You'd forgotten the smell of a working sky.

summary: found the dock flooded with farm-fresh produce from the surface
lines: Harvest shuttles stack the dock with fresh produce — {commodity} at −{discount} for ~{hours}h.
The surface harvest lands and prices sag: {commodity} −{discount}, ~{hours}h.
Crates of the real thing, downwell-fresh: {commodity} going cheap (−{discount}, ~{hours}h).

summary: noticed the station pipes live birdsong up from the surface
lines: The concourse speakers carry live birdsong from downwell. Nobody wants it switched off.
Real dawn chorus, piped 400 klicks up. The station's best feature costs nothing.
Birdsong on the public channel — the planet singing to its station.

summary: walked the fish market that takes up half the lower ring
lines: The lower ring is one vast fish market. The smell arrives two decks early.
Catch from a world-wide sea, iced and shouted over. You buy something with too many fins.
The fishmongers' auction patter is its own dialect. The fish are stranger than the language.

summary: watched a hurricane the size of a continent wheel across the world below
lines: The viewport crowd watches a storm system bigger than nations spiral below.
A hurricane wheels across the ocean world, white and slow and immense.
Downwell, a storm that could swallow coastlines. From up here, lace on the water.

summary: bought a deep-pearl trinket off a diver fresh from the surface
lines: A diver sells pearls from a sea with no bottom on the charts: {credits}.
Deep-pearl, real lustre, fair price: {credits}.
The trinket glows like the sea it came from. You pay {credits} without haggling.

summary: found the surface dust gets onto the station, into everything, regardless
lines: Desert dust on every surface, two hundred klicks above the desert. It finds a way.
The station fights a fine red dust and loses gracefully. Your boots are already ochre.
Dust filters everywhere, dust anyway. The world below insists on being remembered.

summary: overheard the eternal dockside argument about water tariffs
lines: The water tariff argument runs nightly at the cantina. Tonight: episode nine thousand.
Two settlers, one tariff sheet, zero agreement. Desert-world classics.
Water pricing is politics, religion, and sport here. You keep your canteen private.

summary: watched the surface sand-sled races on the cantina screens with the whole dock
lines: Sand-sled season downwell — the cantina backs the orange sail and roars accordingly.
The dune races run all shift on every screen. Productivity dies happy.
A sled flips on the big jump; the bar gasps as one. Racing weather down there.

summary: watched a glacier the size of a city calve on the station's main screen
lines: The survey feed catches a glacier calving — a city's worth of ice, slow as history.
Downwell, ice breaks on a continental scale. The dock watches in respectful silence.
A white cliff the size of a district lets go. Even the dockhands look up.

summary: noticed every table in the cantina has its own heater, by law apparently
lines: Heaters bolted to every cantina table. Ice-world hospitality codes, the barkeep says.
The cold downwell leaks into the architecture: heaters everywhere, blankets on loan.
This station fights the ice-world chill table by table. The cocoa is subsidized.

summary: drank something chilled with hundred-thousand-year-old glacier ice
lines: The bar serves drinks over core-drilled ice older than agriculture. It crackles as it melts.
Ancient ice in a modern glass — the bubbles are fossil air, the barkeep insists.
Glacier-core ice, premium pour. The past melts into your drink, crackling.

summary: queued with everyone else for ash-filter replacements after a surface eruption
lines: Eruption downwell — the whole dock queues for fresh ash filters by midshift.
Filter-change day. The vending machine for them has a line like mail day.
Volcanic ash respects no airlock. New filters, everyone, again.

summary: watched the nightside of the world glow like a banked furnace
lines: The planet's nightside burns dull orange — rivers of fire instead of city lights.
Below, lava veins web the dark hemisphere. Beautiful, the way furnaces are.
No city lights downwell; the ground makes its own. The viewport crowd never thins.

summary: heard the surface foundries are running surplus heats this week
lines: The magma-tap foundries overproduced — {commodity} soft at −{discount} for ~{hours}h.
Surplus heats downwell mean cheap {commodity} upwell: −{discount}, ~{hours}h.
The foundry barges keep coming; {commodity} −{discount} while the docks groan (~{hours}h).

summary: watched the regolith haulers rise from a world with nothing else to give
lines: Haulers lift from the grey world below, full of the only thing it makes: more grey.
Regolith barges on the half-hour, every hour. The world is a quarry with a horizon.
The planet exports dust and silence. Business is steady.

summary: stared a while at a world with no weather, no lights, and no opinion
lines: The world below offers craters, shadows, and absolutely nothing else. Restful, almost.
No clouds, no cities, no change. The barren world is the galaxy's plainest fact.
You watch the airless ground roll by. It has been exactly this for a billion years.

summary: watched the surface crews' low-grav ball league on the dock screens
lines: Quarry-crew ball league tonight — low-grav rules, forty-metre jumps, terrible referee.
The miners play ball in a sixth of a gee. The physics is half the sport.
Surface league finals: a ball hangs in the black sky for nine full seconds. The dock roars.

summary: kept catching the gas giant filling the viewport like a wall of weather
lines: The giant fills every window — banded, vast, indifferent. You keep looking anyway.
No horizon to the planet, just more planet. The viewport feels like a porthole in a dam.
Cloud bands the size of orbits crawl past the docking arm. The station is a mote.

summary: drank with fuel-skimmer pilots who brag in units of atmosphere survived
lines: Skimmer pilots hold court in the cantina — every story is depth, wind shear, and nerve.
The scoop crews measure status in millibars survived. The bar listens and buys.
A skimmer pilot describes riding a thousand-klick wind. Nobody calls it exaggeration twice.

summary: watched an aurora storm wrap the gas giant's pole for hours
lines: The pole lights up — an aurora bigger than worlds, curtains of green a continent tall.
Radiation storm paints the giant's pole. The dock dims its own lights to watch.
Hours of aurora over the pole. The station's cameras can't hold all of it.

summary: studied the promenade shell-game crew long enough to learn the lift
lines: You watch the shell game until the mechanics show. Professional respect, no wager.
The shell crew is good. You clock the palm anyway. Useful, someday.
Twenty minutes of surveillance disguised as spectating. The lift is in the pause.

summary: spotted an easy mark flashing a fat chit, and let it walk
lines: A tourist waves a fat credit chit around. You catalogue and decline. Tonight.
Easy money walks past twice. Discipline holds. Barely.
The mark all but wears a sign. You file the face and order another drink.

summary: papered the dock offices with their contact code, charm set to maximum
lines: Your contact code is now in nine offices and two good pockets. Seeds planted.
A morning of handshakes and follow-ups. Half will forget you. Half is plenty.
You work the offices door to door. The dockmaster's clerk laughs at your joke. Progress.

summary: got recognized by a clerk who remembered the name from somewhere good
lines: The freight clerk knows your name before you give it. The web is working.
'Heard of you,' says the clerk, approvingly. Whatever they heard, it's paying.
Your reputation arrives in rooms before you do now. Cultivate that.

summary: memorized three days of price boards looking for the crack in the market
lines: You can recite the price board from memory now. The pattern is almost visible.
Three days of prices in your head, hunting the seam. It's here somewhere.
The boards rotate; you take notes like a scholar. Bargains favor the prepared.

summary: walked the warehouse rows counting which stacks aren't moving
lines: A slow walk past the warehouses: full racks, no movement. Somebody will crack on price.
You count dust on the cargo stacks. Dusty stock is desperate stock.
Warehouse arithmetic: what sits, sinks. You note three sinking stacks.

summary: got a haircut that makes the security footage somebody else's problem
lines: New cut, new jacket, old face retired. The cameras will need to start over.
The barber asks no questions and takes ten years off the description.
You leave the barber's as a stranger. That was the entire point.

summary: claimed the corner table with the sightlines and stayed there all watch
lines: Back to the wall, eyes on both doors, nursing one drink for three hours. Quiet work.
The corner table sees everything and is seen by nothing. You hold it all watch.
An evening of professional invisibility. The bartender respects the craft.

summary: exchanged the nod with a half-familiar face from a job neither will mention
lines: Across the cantina: a face from an old job. One nod each, full settlement.
You and a stranger agree, wordlessly, that you have never met. Twice now.
Old business walks past in a new coat. The nod says paid in full.

summary: learned which service door on this ring doesn't log its openings
lines: Maintenance door C-31 has a dead logger. Filed under someday.
You find the one door this station forgets. Knowledge with a shelf life — use by trouble.
An unlogged door, a memorized route. You sleep better knowing the exits.

summary: reported a frayed tether line to dock control before it became a headline
lines: You flag a fraying tether to dock control. They fix it within the hour. System works.
One frayed line reported, one accident subtracted from the future.
Dock control logs your hazard report with actual gratitude. Rare, that.

summary: gave a clean witness statement about a loader scrape, to everyone's surprise
lines: A loader clips a strut; you give the statement straight. Both crews blink at the honesty.
Your witness statement contains only what happened. The adjuster rereads it twice.
Just the facts, signed. The insurance clerk frames the novelty.

summary: talked the whole bar into one more round and somehow out of paying for it
lines: By closing, the bar loves you and your tab belongs to a stranger. A gift.
The room orbits your table by the second hour. Drinks materialize.
You tell the one about the customs beagle. The bar buys the next round.

summary: smiled their way into the good berth row without the surcharge
lines: The berth clerk upgrades you to the quiet row, surcharge mysteriously waived.
Five minutes of charm saves a night of turbine lullabies. The good row is yours.
Somehow you're in the premium berths at standard rates. The clerk waves as you pass.

summary: shared two hours and eleven words with the dock's other resident grump
lines: You and the old stevedore drink in industrial-grade silence. Best company in weeks.
Eleven words exchanged across two hours. A rich conversation, by your standards.
The other grump nods at your table. You permit it. The evening passes perfectly.

summary: stared down an upseller until the price returned to the printed one
lines: The vendor's pitch dies under your stare. The printed price suddenly applies.
No, you do not want the extended warranty. Your face says it first.
One look ends the haggle at the listed number. Efficient.

summary: walked the evacuation route to their berth twice, counting hatches
lines: Fourteen hatches between bar and berth, two stick. Now you know which two.
You pace the evac route off the clock. Paranoia is just preparation with a bad reputation.
Escape routes memorized before the second drink. Standard procedure.

summary: re-checked every cargo seal personally despite the dockhand's certificate
lines: The certificate says sealed. You check all of them anyway. One was loose. Always one.
Trust the paperwork; verify the cargo. Twenty minutes well spent.
Every seal pressed by your own thumb. Now it's sealed.

summary: lost a bet about whether the cargo crane could be ridden (it can, briefly)
lines: The crane CAN be ridden, for four seconds. The wager and dignity cost {credits}.
For the record: yes, briefly, then no. The bet settles at {credits}.
Four glorious seconds of crane-riding, priced at {credits}. Worth it. Mostly.

summary: ordered the noodle stand's 'pilot killer' against direct advice
lines: The 'pilot killer' bowl: you finish it. The stand owner takes your photo for the wall.
Against all counsel, the spiciest thing on the ring. Your sinuses file a grievance.
You join the noodle stand's wall of survivors. The aftermath lasts a watch.

summary: hit a vending machine that paid out instead of charging
lines: The vending machine dispenses your snack and {credits} in someone's stuck refunds.
Lucky day: the machine pays YOU ({credits}), plus crackers.
A clunk, a rattle, a jackpot of forgotten change: {credits}.

summary: won the dockworkers' weekly raffle without remembering entering
lines: Your name comes up in the dock raffle. You don't recall buying a ticket. {credits} anyway.
Raffle winner: you, somehow. The pot is {credits} and a commemorative mug.
The dock raffle gods choose you: {credits}. The mug is also yours.

summary: sold a ton of foodstock straight off the ramp to a baker who smelled it arriving
lines: A baker meets the ramp, cash first: 1t of your foodstock for {credits}. No middleman, no forms.
Your flour never touches the warehouse — a baker takes a ton at the ramp for {credits}.
Ramp-side deal: one ton of food, {credits}, and a warm loaf on the handshake.

summary: stood through the port vet's inspection of the livestock hold
lines: The port vet inspects your livestock with terrifying thoroughness. All cleared, all judged.
Forty minutes of vet inspection. The animals pass; your stall hygiene gets notes.
Livestock certified healthy. The vet's expression suggests you barely passed as owner.

summary: had the mineral cargo assayed by a prospector who missed the trade
lines: A retired prospector assays your minerals for the love of it. 'Decent grade,' — high praise.
Free assay from an old rock-hound: your ore is exactly what you paid for. Reassuring.
The prospector reads your minerals like tea leaves. Verdict: honest cargo.

summary: caught a station kid reading the spec sheets on the electronics crates like comics
lines: A kid memorizes your electronics manifests through the webbing. Future engineer, or thief.
The crate labels have a fan: one kid, two hours, total absorption.
You explain what a phase regulator does. The kid corrects you. Fair enough.

summary: passed the port medic's cold-chain spot check on the medical cargo
lines: Cold-chain inspection on the medical crates: temperatures logged, seals intact, medic satisfied.
The port medic audits your reefer readouts. Green across the board.
Medical cargo checked crate by crate. The medic signs off and tips an imaginary hat.

summary: rented a crated lifter to a shorthanded stevedore gang for the afternoon
lines: Your crated lifter earns its passage: an afternoon's rental to the stevedores, {credits}.
The gang next berth borrows your equipment for {credits} and returns it cleaner.
Idle cargo, working capital: {credits} in rental for the lifter.

summary: got photographed by core tourists as 'local dock color'
lines: A tour group photographs you loading cargo. You are now somebody's vacation.
Core tourists, matching hats, forty cameras. The dock is today's exhibit. You're in it.
'Act natural,' says the tour guide, pointing at you. You gesture rudely. They love it.

summary: read a bronze plaque marking three centuries of continuous dock operations
lines: Three hundred years of dockings, says the plaque. The deck plates believe it.
This port is older than some worlds' charts. The plaque wears its dates like medals.
Continuous operation since before the rim had names. Core space remembers long.

summary: compared hand-corrected charts with other rim captains over the table
lines: Chart night: rim captains pencil corrections the cartographers won't have for years.
Out here the charts are folklore plus corrections. You copy three and contribute one.
Somebody's hand-drawn lane note saves somebody else's hull. Frontier cartography.

summary: read the bounty board, which out here is longer than the menu
lines: The bounty board runs to three columns. The rim polices itself, cash on delivery.
Wanted notices, salvage claims, one apology note. The rim's classified ads.
You read the bounty board for names you know. Two. You say nothing.

summary: noted the sign that says LAST RELIABLE FUEL and means it
lines: LAST RELIABLE FUEL FOR SIX SECTORS, says the sign. Out here, that's not marketing.
The fuel gauge sign is hand-painted and dead serious. Beyond this port: hope.
You top off everything that holds charge. The sign has earned its capital letters.

summary: watched the ship's cat pass its own customs inspection with full honors
lines: Customs inspects the cat. The cat inspects customs. Both pass, the cat with distinction.
The cat's import paperwork is somehow in better order than yours.
An officer scans the cat, who permits it regally. Cleared for all decks.

summary: found the ship's cat holding court on the cantina bar two hours after sneaking out
lines: The cat beat you to the cantina and has a stool, a saucer, and a following.
Your cat is on the bar being adored by strangers. It pretends not to know you.
Cat located: cantina, centre stage, milk provided. It left without telling you.

summary: let the dockside bone-setter work on the bruised ribs, regretting and appreciating it
lines: The dock masseur finds every bruise and introduces them to each other. It helps. Eventually.
Ten minutes of percussive therapy on the ribs. You leave sore in a more organized way.
The bone-setter's verdict: 'You'll live.' The technique suggests this was negotiable.

summary: got a generous amount of personal space on account of the visible spots
lines: The spots clear a two-metre radius in any crowd. Quarantine etiquette, rim style.
Your measles get you a whole table to yourself. Silver linings, freckle-shaped.
The barkeep serves you at arm's length plus a broom handle. Fair.

summary: logged a micrometeor ping off the hull, more greeting than threat
lines: A micrometeor taps the hull — one bright ping, logged and forgotten.
Something the size of a rice grain says hello at orbital velocity. The plating shrugs.
Ping. The void's way of checking you're awake.

summary: listened to the hull tick as it cooled into the shadow side of the orbit
lines: The ship crosses into shadow and the hull ticks itself cool, old song, every orbit.
Thermal tick-tick-tick down the spine as the sun drops behind the world.
Shadow side: the hull contracts, creaking like a settling house.

summary: scrubbed the galley to parade standard for no reason except time
lines: The galley now gleams. At anchor, cleanliness is what ambition turns into.
Two hours, one sponge, total victory over the galley. The void provides time.
You deep-clean the galley and reorganize the spice tin. Anchor watch does this to people.

summary: re-inventoried the hold and found it exactly as inventoried
lines: Full hold count: everything precisely where the manifest claims. Satisfying, somehow.
You audit your own cargo for sport. The books balance. The afternoon passes.
Inventory complete. Discrepancies: zero. Pride: moderate.

summary: watched the terminator line crawl across the world below
lines: Dawn crawls across the planet in real time — a line of fire eating the dark.
You watch sunrise happen to an entire hemisphere. It takes an hour and earns it.
The terminator sweeps below, dragging morning behind it.

summary: drifted past the local satellite graveyard, all dead lights and good bones
lines: The graveyard orbit slides past: dead satellites, neat rows, decades of quiet.
Old satellites tumble slow in their parking orbit. Some still blink, out of habit.
A museum nobody visits, orbiting forever. You pay respects on the way by.

summary: watched the docking queue perform its slow choreography below
lines: Freighters queue for the station in stately order — a ballet measured in kilometres.
The approach lanes weave traffic like clockwork. From anchor, it's hypnotic.
You watch the docking queue the way some people watch fires.

summary: finally answered the message backlog, oldest and most embarrassing first
lines: Anchor watch: the message backlog falls, oldest debts of correspondence first.
You answer a message from four ports ago. The apology paragraph writes itself.
Inbox zero achieved somewhere over the nightside. Witnessed only by the void.

summary: lost a fight with a coffee bulb in zero-g and wore the evidence
lines: The coffee bulb's valve fails; the galaxy gains a small brown nebula. You wear some.
Coffee, liberated, explores the cabin. Cleanup eats half a watch.
Zero-g coffee incident #7. The console survives. The shirt does not.

summary: renamed the brighter stars out the viewport after old crewmates
lines: You give the bright stars old crewmates' names. They'd argue about which got which.
An hour of private astronomy, naming stars for people who'd laugh at the honor.
The constellations out here are yours to invent. You people them with familiar faces.

summary: watched the nightside cities below come on like slow constellations
lines: The nightside rolls under — cities lighting up in webs and rivers of gold.
Below, a hemisphere's worth of evenings begin. The lights map every harbor and road.
City glow traces the coastlines under you. A living world, leaving its lamps on.

summary: tracked a tidy weather front bringing rain to somebody's growing season
lines: A rain front crosses the farm belt below, right on schedule. Lucky planet.
You watch weather being useful for once — rain arriving where the green is.
Clouds queue along the coast like freight. The fields below are about to drink.

summary: orbited above a storm spiral wider than some moons
lines: The storm below has an eye you could lose a moon in. It turns, slow and white.
One spiral of cloud owns a quarter of the visible sea. You cross it for an hour.
The ocean world wears its hurricane like a brooch the size of a sky.

summary: caught a bioluminescent bloom tracing the currents of the nightside sea
lines: The nightside sea glows — plankton bloom riding the currents in green script.
Below, the ocean writes in cold light. Whole currents luminous from orbit.
Bioluminescence sketches the gyres under you. The planet showing its handwriting.

summary: watched a dust storm swallow a third of the visible hemisphere
lines: A wall of ochre crosses the desert world, eating canyons whole.
The dust storm below is continental and unhurried. Nothing down there argues with it.
By the second orbit the storm owns the hemisphere. The desert rearranges itself.

summary: watched dawn stretch dune shadows a hundred kilometres long
lines: Low sun over the ergs: dune shadows like claw marks across the world.
Dawn makes the desert below all texture — a hundred-klick comb of light and dark.
The dunes throw shadows long enough to chart. Morning on a dry world.

summary: flew through the upper fringe of an aurora over the ice world's pole
lines: The polar aurora reaches up past your orbit — you fly through the hem of it.
Green curtains over the ice cap, close enough to touch the instruments.
Aurora below, aurora around. The ice world wears its crown high tonight.

summary: squinted against a whole world's worth of sunrise glare off the ice
lines: Sunrise off the ice sheet: the planet becomes a mirror and the viewport gives up.
The dayside glare could navigate by. White world, full albedo, polarizers earning their keep.
An entire hemisphere of fresh snow catches the sun. You orbit a lamp.

summary: watched a new eruption stitch a glowing seam across the nightside
lines: A fissure opens on the nightside — a fresh seam of orange, kilometres a minute.
Eruption below: the dark hemisphere gains a new river of light while you watch.
The planet redecorates in molten strokes. The seismograph feed is a drumroll.

summary: tracked an ash plume punching clean through the cloud deck
lines: An ash column climbs past the weather and keeps going. The volcano means it.
One plume rises pole-straight through the entire atmosphere. Respect.
Ash to the edge of space. Your orbit gets a dusting warning.

summary: read the crater shadows below like the world's only diary
lines: Crater rims catch the low sun — four billion years of bad days, neatly recorded.
The barren world's history is all impacts. Dawn makes every entry legible.
Shadows pool in craters older than oceans elsewhere. Quiet reading.

summary: orbited across an impact ring big enough to have its own horizon
lines: One ancient impact ring spans the viewport edge to edge. The scar outlived the wound.
A ringwall crosses below for ten full minutes. Something enormous happened here once.
The old basin swallows the view: rim mountains, frozen shock, dead centre peak.

summary: kept anchor watch over a storm that has outlived nations
lines: The great storm turns below — older than charts, wider than worlds, utterly unbothered.
You orbit a storm with a proper name and a measured age in centuries.
The anticyclone stares up like an eye. You blink first. Every time.

summary: watched a moon transit the gas giant's face, a coin crossing a wall
lines: A moon crosses the giant's face — a fleck of rock against a continent of cloud.
Transit below: one moon, one shadow, one absurd difference in scale.
The moon's shadow skates across the cloud bands. Perspective, served cold.

summary: monitored the station's security band getting steadily less boring below
lines: The security band below crackles all watch — codes you don't know, tones you do.
Down on the station, something's winding tight. At anchor, you get the radio version.
You keep half an ear on the law channel. It's having a busy night down there.

summary: counted thirty ships stacked in the approach queue for one rich port
lines: Thirty hulls hold pattern below you. The port's too rich to land at, almost.
The approach queue glitters all the way down — boom-time traffic, stacked deep.
Holding ships in every parking shell. Prosperity has a traffic problem.

summary: noted that out here, theirs is the only running light in the whole sky
lines: No other lights at anchor tonight. The rim's sky is yours alone.
One ship, one world, no neighbors for an audit's worth of distance. The quiet has texture.
You kill the cabin lamps and let the frontier dark in for a while.

summary: shared the viewport with the cat, who watched the world turn like it owed rent
lines: The cat takes the viewport sill and audits the planet below. Verdict pending.
Two of you on anchor watch now. The cat takes the world; you take the instruments.
The cat stares down the planet for a full hour. The planet blinks first, presumably.

summary: ran the lane's buoy chain, each beacon handing the ship to the next
lines: Buoy to buoy down the lane, each one pinging you onward like a relay of lighthouses.
The lane markers count you through the dark. Seventeen, eighteen, nineteen.
Every few minutes a buoy blinks past, keeping the void honest.

summary: got three chapters deeper into the audiobook that has outlasted four routes
lines: Three more chapters fall to the long haul. The narrator is family by now.
The audiobook resumes where the last course left it. The plot and the lane both drag on agreeably.
Chapter forty-one. You no longer remember buying this book. You'll finish it anyway.

summary: spent an hour tuning the drive harmonics by ear, like it matters
lines: You chase a half-tone wobble in the drive song for an hour. Victory: it's a quarter-tone now.
Drive harmonics, tuned by ear and stubbornness. The hum sits right at last.
The engine's pitch was bothering you. Now it isn't. The log calls this 'maintenance.'

summary: conducted a formal ranking of the ration flavors; 'beef' placed last again
lines: Mid-haul cuisine review: 'chicken' holds first, 'beef' defends last place successfully.
You rank the rations again. The order never changes. The ritual matters anyway.
Dinner: ration pack #4, reviewed harshly, eaten entirely.

summary: re-ran the course numbers and saved a theoretical four minutes
lines: Two hours of optimization buys four minutes of arrival. The math was the fun part.
You shave the course by a rounding error and feel like a navigator of old.
Course refined. ETA improves imperceptibly. Worth it.

summary: answered a hail from a dead satellite still doing its job after decades
lines: A derelict relay pings you its weather report. The weather is from thirty years ago.
Dead satellite, live transmitter: it logs your passage like it logged a thousand others.
Something old and faithful blinks at you from the dark and goes back to waiting.

summary: paced a slowly tumbling asteroid for a few hundred klicks
lines: An asteroid keeps loose formation with you for an hour, turning over like a sleeper.
Company on the lane: one rock, tumbling slow, going your way for a while.
The asteroid drifts off course eventually. You log the parting like a goodbye.

summary: did the full resistance-band routine for once, every set, no skipping
lines: The exercise bands come out and, miracle, the whole routine gets done.
Mid-course fitness: every set completed. The log entry is half boast.
You finish the resistance routine the medic prescribed. Smugness: earned.

summary: reread old log entries and barely recognized the trader who wrote them
lines: Old logs on the long haul: the rookie who wrote them worried about everything. Some of it mattered.
You scroll your own history between hops. The handwriting's the same; the nerve isn't.
Three-year-old log entries. You'd like to buy that earlier self a drink and a clue.

summary: let the open channel's static wash the cabin like rain on a roof
lines: Empty band, pure static, volume low — the void's own white noise machine.
You leave the dead channel open. The hiss is better company than silence.
Static on the long watch, soft as weather. The cabin breathes with it.

summary: patched a micrometeor scuff before it could become a story
lines: A grain of the void scuffs the hull; sealant and patience fix it: {credits}.
Hull patch on the move — small hole, smaller drama, {credits} in sealant.
Micrometeor kiss, patched within the hour: {credits} in consumables.

summary: watched a distant star flare, brighten, and think better of it
lines: Off the port bow, a star flares briefly brighter — a candle guttering somewhere unthinkable.
The nav computer flags a stellar flare, light-years off. The sky's own weather.
A pinpoint in the black doubles its shine for a minute. You alone applaud.

summary: passed a grain convoy running nose-to-tail like beads on a wire
lines: A convoy slides past the other way — six hulls, one course, zero conversation.
Grain haulers in formation, nose to tail. You exchange transponder courtesies and nothing else.
The convoy's running lights string the dark like a slow constellation.

summary: got a courtesy wing-rock from a bored patrol cutter on a safe lane
lines: A patrol cutter slides by and rocks its wings. Core lanes: the law waves hello.
The patrol's scan is a formality; the wave afterward is genuine. Quiet lane, easy company.
Security out here is a friendly silhouette and a clean transponder ping.

summary: shared the lane with school shuttles and commuter packets, of all things
lines: A school shuttle crosses your lane, full of waving kids. Deep core, safe as houses.
Commuter traffic on the lane — the safest sky there is, and it looks it.
You queue behind a packet bus at the lane merge. Civilization, dense and unbothered.

summary: passed a marked wreck, transponder still pleading on the emergency band
lines: A charted wreck slides by, beacon still calling. The date in its loop is years old.
Wreck marker on the lane. You note its silence beneath the automated distress loop.
The hulk's transponder still asks for help on schedule. Nobody's left to cancel it.

summary: chased a distress echo two points off course before it proved decades old
lines: A distress ghost on the band — bearing checked, archive checked: a recording older than you.
You vector toward a mayday that turns out to be the lane's resident echo. Every captain falls for it once.
The famous false mayday of this stretch claims another sympathetic course check.

summary: caught gun-camera bragging on the open band from someone's bad night
lines: Somebody streams gun-camera footage on the open band. You note the lane it happened on. It's this one.
The pirate band brags in grainy video tonight. You adjust nothing, visibly. Speed, slightly.
Combat footage crackles past on an open channel — last week, this stretch. You fly politely.

summary: ran the worst stretch dark, comms cold, the old rim way
lines: Running lights off, transponder coy, reactor whisper-quiet. The rim teaches its etiquette fast.
You fly this stretch the way the old hands do: dark, quick, and unmemorable.
Cold comms through the bad zone. The silence out here is procedure, not mood.

summary: scrubbed the drive signature mid-course out of well-earned paranoia
lines: An hour venting heat and trimming the drive plume. Out here, a clean signature is a kindness to yourself.
You make the ship boring to every sensor in range. The rim rewards boring.
Signature scrubbed to a whisper. Whatever hunts this stretch will need better eyes.

summary: declined a freelance 'escort' offer that smelled like the toll it was
lines: A gunship offers 'protective escort' at friendly rates. You decline at unfriendly speed.
Escort services on the worst lane in the chart: the protection racket grows wings out here.
'For your safety,' says the gunship. For your wallet, says the tone. You pass.

summary: flew off the edge of the reliable charts and onto the dotted lines
lines: The chart's confidence interval widens with every hop. Out here the map is a rumor.
Past this buoy the survey data is older than the buoy. You trust the instruments and the gut, in that order.
The nav display starts hedging — dotted lanes, estimated hazards, honest ignorance.

summary: passed the last maintained beacon and gave it a nod on the way by
lines: The last serviced beacon on the route blinks you past. Beyond it: best wishes.
One final lighthouse, then the long dark. You log its number with something like affection.
The beacon's plate says MAINTAINED BY VOLUNTEERS. Out here, that's infrastructure.

summary: tracked a light on the scope that the charts insist cannot be there
lines: A flicker on the scope where the chart shows nothing. It does not repeat. You log it anyway.
Something blinks, once, in a sector the survey calls empty. The rim keeps its secrets.
Unexplained contact, one ping, gone. Out here the charts are suggestions and the dark is roomy.

summary: walked the hull seals twice between hops, because twice is the right number
lines: Mid-course seal inspection, both passes clean. The ritual stands.
Every gasket checked between jumps. Paranoia: zero findings, full satisfaction.
You walk the seals again. The ship is tight. Now you know, instead of believing.

summary: shaved the course past a gravity well close enough to feel the tug
lines: You cut the corner past the well close enough that the coffee leans. Time saved: minutes. Grin: full.
The safe lane bends wide; you don't. The hull groans agreeably at the slingshot.
Gravity-assist by audacity. The nav computer files a formal sigh.

summary: found a credit chip from some previous occupant wedged under the seat rail
lines: Cleaning the cockpit turns up a stranger's credit chip under the rail: {credits}.
A previous owner's loose change surfaces mid-flight: {credits}.
The seat rail has been hoarding {credits} since before you owned the ship.

summary: hosted an hour of impromptu talk-show on the long-range band
lines: You open the long-range band and hold court — three ships, two time zones, one good hour.
An hour of lane-talk radio, hosted by you. The regulars request an encore at the next dead stretch.
Your voice keeps four lonely cockpits company across the dark. Tips accepted in gossip.

summary: switched the comms to standby and enjoyed the void's one great virtue
lines: Comms to standby. The void delivers its finest feature: nobody.
Eight hours, zero conversations. The long haul, perfected.
You and the engine hum, and that's the whole guest list. Excellent.

summary: spent a fragrant hour mucking out the livestock hold mid-course
lines: The livestock hold demands its hourly diplomacy. You emerge victorious and fragrant.
Mid-course barn chores. The animals are fine. The boots are a loss.
Feeding, watering, shoveling — the cargo that talks back gets full service.

summary: flew the whole leg inside the smell of the grain in the hold
lines: The whole ship smells of the grain cargo — bakery air at one gee of thrust.
Foodstock in the hold perfumes every deck. The rations taste worse by comparison.
You haul the smell of harvest through the void. Not the worst company.

summary: tracked down a chirp in the hold to a crate of electronics self-testing
lines: A mystery chirp turns out to be the electronics cargo running its own diagnostics. Smug crates.
Hour three of the hunt: the chirp is crate 12, testing itself and passing.
The cargo beeps contentedly to itself all leg. You stop hearing it eventually.

summary: sprinted to a cold-chain alarm that turned out to be a sensor's bad dream
lines: The reefer alarm screams; the medicine is fine; the sensor gets reseated firmly.
Cold-chain false alarm at 0300 ship time. Heart rate: also alarmed. Cargo: serene.
One faulty probe, one unnecessary sprint, zero spoiled crates. Acceptable.
